title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and seasons, describe nature, and say what is about to happen or looks likely.
intro:
The Telugu states have three real seasons: a fierce **summer** (*వేసవి*, March–June, often above 40°C), the **monsoon** (*వర్షాకాలం*, June–September, with cyclones on the coast in autumn) and a mild **winter** (*చలికాలం*).

Weather is described with verbs of falling and blowing (*వర్షం పడుతోంది*, rain is falling) or with *-గా ఉంది* (*చలిగా ఉంది*, it's cold). To say something is about to happen, Telugu uses *-బోతోంది*.

vocab.note: Colloquially వాన (vāna); pl. వర్షాలు = the rains
The Godavari and Krishna are the great Telugu rivers.
గాలి వీస్తోంది, the wind is blowing

phrases.en: The rains were good this year.
Look at the stars in the sky!
What's the name of this flower?

grammar.title: Talking about the weather
grammar.body:
Telugu weather sentences have no dummy 'it'. Two patterns cover almost everything:
1. **Noun + verb**: rain *falls* (*వర్షం పడుతోంది*), wind *blows* (*గాలి వీస్తోంది*), sun *shines/burns* (*ఎండ కాస్తోంది*), thunder *rumbles* (*ఉరుముతోంది*).
2. **Noun + -గా ఉంది**: *చలిగా ఉంది* (it's cold), *ఎండగా ఉంది* (it's sunny), *ఉక్కగా ఉంది* (it's muggy), *మబ్బుగా ఉంది* (it's cloudy).

For general truths, use the non-past *ఉంటుంది*: *వేసవిలో వేడిగా ఉంటుంది* (it's [usually] hot in summer). Add the dative for how *you* feel: *నాకు చలిగా ఉంది* (I'm cold).

grammar.title: About to happen, looks likely: -బోతు-, -ఏలా ఉంది
grammar.body:
**About to / going to**: infinitive stem in -a + **బోతు-** + person ending: *పడబోతోంది* (is about to fall), *వెళ్ళబోతున్నాను* (I'm about to go / I'm going to go). It suggests something imminent or planned.

**Looks like**: future relative form + **-లా ఉంది**: *వర్షం వచ్చేలా ఉంది* (it looks like rain).

**Reported information**: add **-అట** (-aṭa, 'they say') to a sentence: *రేపు తుఫాను వస్తుందట* (apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow). Very common for news and gossip.

examples.en: Apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow.
They say this summer will be very hot.

dialogue.title: Storm clouds
dialogue.setting: Two colleagues, Naveen and Sunitha, are leaving the office in the evening.

lines.speaker: Naveen
lines.en: Look outside, the sky is black.

lines.speaker: Naveen
lines.en: They said on TV a cyclone is coming tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Sunitha
lines.en: Oh no! I don't have an umbrella.

lines.speaker: Naveen
lines.native: పర్వాలేదు, నా దగ్గర రెండు ఉన్నాయి. ఒకటి తీసుకో.
lines.roman: parvālēdu, nā daggara reṇḍu unnāyi. okaṭi tīsukō.
lines.en: No problem, I have two. Take one.

lines.speaker: Sunitha
lines.native: థాంక్స్. మొన్నటి వరకు ఎండలు, ఇప్పుడు వర్షాలు!
lines.roman: thāṅks. monnaṭi varaku eṇḍalu, ippuḍu varṣālu!
lines.en: Thanks. Scorching heat until the other day, and now rain!

lines.speaker: Naveen
lines.native: అదే మంచిది. పొలాలకి నీళ్ళు కావాలి కదా.
lines.roman: adē manchidi. polālaki nīḷḷu kāvāli kadā.
lines.en: That's a good thing. The fields need water, don't they.

lines.speaker: Sunitha
lines.en: True. Let's get home before it rains.

culture: Agriculture still shapes Telugu life: the coastal Godavari and Krishna deltas are the 'rice bowl' of India, and a good monsoon is front-page news. Summer (*ఎండాకాలం*) brings mango season, with Banganapalle mangoes and the famous *ఆవకాయ* (raw-mango pickle) made in every home. Cyclones from the Bay of Bengal strike the Andhra coast most years between October and December.

tip.title: It's cold, it's sunny: noun + -గా ఉంది
tip.body:
- Telugu has no 'it' for weather. Add **-గా ఉంది** to the noun: చలి → **చలిగా ఉంది** 'it's cold', ఎండ → **ఎండగా ఉంది** 'it's sunny', మబ్బు → **మబ్బుగా ఉంది** 'it's cloudy'.
- How *you* feel takes the dative: **మీకు** చలిగా ఉందా? 'are you cold?'
- Usually / in general: **ఉంటుంది** instead of ఉంది.

sentences.en: It's very cold today.
Is it sunny outside?
It's cloudy today.

sentences.native: ఇక్కడ చాలా ఉక్కగా ఉంది, ఫ్యాను వేయండి.
sentences.roman: ikkaḍa chālā ukkagā undi, phyānu vēyaṇḍi.
sentences.en: It's really muggy in here, put the fan on.
Are you cold?
It's cold here in the mornings.
The sun is really strong.
Don't go wandering about in the sun.
The weather's nice, let's go out.

tip.title: Rain falls, wind blows
tip.body:
- Rain *falls*: **వర్షం పడుతోంది** 'it's raining'. Wind *blows*: **గాలి వీస్తోంది**.
- -తోంది is the spoken '-ing' form for it/she: పడు**తోంది**, వీస్**తోంది**, ఉరుము**తోంది** 'it's thundering'.
- వర్షం and వాన both mean rain; వాన is more everyday.

sentences.en: Is it raining?
A cool breeze is blowing.
It's been raining since the morning.
It's raining, take an umbrella.
It's thundering, don't go out. (to a friend)
There's no breeze, it's really muggy.
Look at the lightning!
Has the rain eased off?
Where's my umbrella?

tip.title: What it's usually like: ఉంటుంది
tip.body:
- For what a season is *usually* like, use the non-past: వేసవిలో వేడిగా **ఉంటుంది**.
- With plural things: ఎండలు ఎక్కువగా **ఉంటాయి**, తుఫానులు **వస్తాయి**.
- 'In' a season is **-లో**: వేసవి**లో**, చలికాలం**లో**.

sentences.en: It's very cold here in winter.
In the rainy season it rains every day.
The heat is fierce in summer.
Cyclones are common here.
What's summer like in your home town?
The roads are bad in the rainy season.
I don't like summer.
Which season should I come in?
Winter is lovely.

tip.title: Plurals that change shape
tip.body:
- Most nouns just add **-లు**: చుక్క → **చుక్కలు**, ఆకు → **ఆకులు**, మబ్బు → **మబ్బులు**.
- Some squeeze: చెట్టు → **చెట్లు** (not చెట్టులు).
- Some change: పువ్వు → **పూలు**.
- Plural things take **ఉన్నాయి** / **లేవు**: చుక్కలు ఉన్నాయి, మబ్బులు లేవు.

sentences.native: మా ఇంటి ముందు రెండు చెట్లు ఉన్నాయి.
sentences.roman: mā iṇṭi mundu reṇḍu cheṭlu unnāyi.
sentences.en: There are two trees in front of our house.
These flowers are very beautiful.
There are no clouds in the sky.
This tree's leaves are big.
There are lots of stars in the sky tonight.
Mum loves flowers.
This tree is very big.
Look how beautiful the moon is!
In the evening the sun is red.

tip.title: About to, looks like, apparently
tip.body:
- About to / going to: stem + **-బోతు-**: రా**బోతోంది** 'is about to come', వెళ్ళ**బోతున్నాం** 'we're going to go'.
- Looks like: **-ఏలా ఉంది**: వాన **వచ్చేలా ఉంది** 'looks like rain'; ఆగేలా **లేదు** 'doesn't look like stopping'.
- They say / apparently: add **-అట**: ఉంటుంది → ఉంటుంద**ట**.

sentences.en: Look at the clouds, it looks like rain.
It doesn't look like the rain will stop.
A cyclone is about to hit.
We're going to the hills next week.
Dad is about to go to the field.

sentences.native: రేపు సముద్రం దగ్గర గాలి ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుందట.
sentences.roman: rēpu samudram daggara gāli ekkuvagā uṇṭundaṭa.
sentences.en: They say it'll be very windy by the sea tomorrow.

sentences.native: ఈ ఏడాది నదిలో నీళ్ళు బాగా ఉన్నాయట.
sentences.roman: ī ēḍādi nadilō nīḷḷu bāgā unnāyaṭa.
sentences.en: Apparently there's plenty of water in the river this year.
They say that forest is huge.
The soil here is very red.
Shall we go to the seaside on Sunday?
